directions: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in consistently moist to wet, fertile soil in full sun, spacing plants at least 3 feet apart to allow for their tall, upright growth. This white-flowered form of the scarlet swamp mallow is otherwise identical to the species in habit and vigor, producing pure white, five-petaled, dinner-plate-sized blooms with a deep red or maroon throat on 5 to 8 foot stems above deeply lobed, palmate foliage from midsummer through early fall. Keep the root zone saturated during the growing season, especially in hot weather, and cut old stems to the ground after they die back in winter since new growth emerges from the crown each spring. Excellent for pond margins, rain gardens, and wet low spots where its bright white flowers show up dramatically against dark green foliage.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or plant container-grown stock in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Jackman's Variety is one of the older, more vigorous yellow-flowered selections, with larger leaves and blooms than the wild species.

directions: Plant in full sun in average to lean, well-drained soil in spring, spacing plants 3 to 4 feet apart to give this vigorous, rounded shrub room to fill out. Jackman's Variety bears bright golden-yellow, single flowers roughly 1.5 inches across in great profusion from June through September, standing out for its larger flower size and darker green foliage compared to many other Potentilla fruticosa cultivars. It tolerates heat, drought, poor soil, alkaline pH, and light shearing extremely well once established, making it a durable choice for hedges, foundation plantings, and mass borders. Prune out about a third of the oldest stems every few years in late winter to renew flowering wood and keep the shrub from becoming twiggy at the base.

common_name: Katherine Dykes Potentilla (Pale Yellow Shrubby Cinquefoil)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or plant container-grown stock in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Katherine Dykes has a graceful, arching, wide-spreading habit and fine gray-green foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in average, well-drained soil in spring, giving this cultivar extra lateral room since it typically spreads wider than it grows tall. Katherine Dykes produces soft, pale primrose-yellow flowers continuously from late spring into fall on gracefully arching branches clothed in fine, silvery-green, needle-like leaflets, making it a good choice for informal hedges, slopes, and mixed borders where a fountain-like form is desirable. It is very drought and heat tolerant once established and needs little supplemental water beyond an occasional deep soak in extended dry spells. Rejuvenate older plants by removing a portion of the oldest woody stems at ground level every few years in late winter to keep flowering vigorous.

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or plant container-grown stock in well-drained soil in full sun with some afternoon shade in hot climates; Red Ace was one of the first orange-red flowered cinquefoil cultivars and holds its color best where summers are cool.

directions: Plant in spring in average, well-drained soil, choosing a site with full morning sun and light afternoon shade in hot-summer regions to preserve the best flower color. Red Ace forms a low, dense, compact mound bearing orange-red flowers with a yellow reverse and yellow centers; the vivid orange-red color is most intense in cool spring and fall weather and tends to fade toward yellowish-orange during peak summer heat. It is a good choice for the front of borders, low informal hedging, or mass plantings where its compact size and long bloom season from late spring to early fall are assets. Water regularly the first year to establish, then reduce to occasional deep watering during dry spells, and trim lightly after the first flush to encourage rebloom.

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings in early summer or plant container-grown stock in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Gold Drop (sometimes sold as 'Farreri') is valued for its fine, small-leaved texture and compact, dense habit.

directions: Plant in full sun in average, well-drained soil in spring, spacing plants about 2 feet apart for a tidy, low, dense mass. Gold Drop is prized for its small, finely divided leaflets that give the whole plant a delicate, ferny texture, contrasted with an abundance of small, bright golden-yellow flowers produced from late spring through early fall. Its compact, rounded habit makes it well suited to rock gardens, low edging, and small-space plantings where larger cinquefoil cultivars would be out of scale. It tolerates heat, drought, and poor rocky soil once established, and benefits from an occasional light shearing after the first bloom flush to maintain its dense form and encourage continued flowering.
